messages.subject: distsamp() function
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to use the package “unmarked” under R, and especially the distsamp() function following the paper written by Richard Chandler (January 13, 2014). I have no problem having the data imported, formatted and summarized, and my histogram of detection distances is ok. However, when I want to fit the model: hn_Null<-distsamp(~1~1,umf) I get the error: "Hessian is singular. Try using fewer covariates or providing starting values." I can’t figure why! I have 7 transect, around 60 species and more than 3000 observations. I have no transect-specific covariates. My data has the form:

messages.author: f0732d7bffc290cf
messages.subject: summarizing trends over a higher grouping level than primary period
parts:
Hi all,
I am currently working on some nocturnal forest mammal data (from
spotlight surveys) using pcountOPEN. I have 35 primary periods (defined
by year/season combinations) as that was the period in which I felt it
reasonable to assume closure. However, I am really interested in
differences between two longer time-periods distinguished before and
after primary period 16 or so. ("time_step3" in my model). This may be
a simple question, but is there are recommended way to summarize such
population trends at a higher level than primary period perhaps using
the yearlySiteCovs? an example model looks like this:

(fm37a <- pcountOpen(~MATemp+MATemp2+annual_pptn12, ~time_step3,
~time_step3,
~wet+wind+season+temp_anomaly+moon+decimal_start, spp.umf,
K=tk,mixture = "ZIP", dynamics = "constant", se =
TRUE))
